opening.argument: The segment identifies a reported gift-card barcode-substitution scheme through an investigative news format, beginning with the framing “I-Team: Scammers Target Gift Cards” and describing how alleged crooks created another way to steal money. It explains that a barcode was taped over a nonworking Walmart barcode and that $500 was activated on that substituted barcode, making the mechanism concrete for viewers. The segment then turns to prevention: it advises rubbing a nail across the barcode to check that it is raised and keeping the activation receipt for reference. Its closing warning says, “Don't be a victim,” and the segment does not show the creators asking viewers for payment, credentials, or participation in the described mechanism.

citations.quote: The Fox 5's I-team's Dana Fallows here with how crooks have created another way to steal your money
Kroger recommends rubbing a nail across that barcode to make sure it's raised.
Also make sure your gift recipient has that activation receipt for reference.
Buyer Beware, letting her circle of friends know there's a new scam in town. Don't be a victim.
